Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps around encryption and key management.

Recap:
- In-transit: All traffic to Redwood is protected with TLS 1.2+ (we are TLS 1.3-ready in our hosted env).
- At-rest: Data is encrypted using AES-256-GCM; we use envelope encryption (data key encrypted with a root/master key).
- KMS options: We support Redwood-managed keys (default), Customer-Managed Keys (CMEK) via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault), and Dedicated HSM/Bring-Your-Own-Key for Private deployments.
- Logging & retention: Request/response logging is configurable; sensitive fields can be redacted and payload logging disabled for regulated workloads. Retention windows are configurable per-account.
- Residency: We can pin data to US, EU, or APAC regions depending on deployment.

Answers to the questions you raised on the call:
1) BYOK vs CMEK: For hosted customers we support CMEK where you provide the master key in your cloud KMS and Redwood uses that key to encrypt the data encryption keys. For stricter requirements we offer an HSM-backed option in Dedicated or Private deployments where keys never leave the HSM under customer control (supports PKCS#11/EKM flows).
2) Key rotation & SLA: Customer-managed keys remain under your control; rotation operations are initiated through your KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure). We rotate data/DEKs annually by default but can align rotations with your policies.
3) Logging of plaintext: We do not persist plaintext model inputs in long-term logs by default. We can turn off request payload logging entirely and provide redacted observability if needed.
4) Audit evidence: We can provide scoped audit bundles and our SOC 2 Type II report once NDA is in place.

Attachments: redwood_spec_kms_options.pdf (high-level options), SOC2-brief.pdf (summary). I also pasted a short proposed next-steps list below.

Proposed next steps:
- Share full security questionnaire (you to send existing doc) — Alice / Paywise Sec Team
- Technical deep-dive on CMEK/HSM and integration plan (30–45 min) — schedule this week if possible
- Confirm retention requirements and whether you need payload logging disabled
- If satisfied, move to procurement + add CMEK clause in SOW (we can draft)

Would Thursday 10:00 AM PT work for an engineering deep-dive?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Hi Alice — answering the technical pieces here, happy to cover more on the call.

1) AWS KMS CMEK details:
- We support AWS KMS CMEK for hosted customers where you provide a key ARN. Redwood never has access to your KMS master key (we call KMS APIs using a customer-created IAM role that you provision).
- Imported key material: supported where the customer uploads key material to their KMS and grants Redwood use permissions.

2) HSM/BYOK:
- For Private/Dedicated, we support HSM-backed keys and PKCS#11-based connectors. We can integrate with on-prem HSMs or cloud HSM services; keys can be configured to never leave the HSM.
- KMIP/EKM-supported integrations available for dedicated/private installs.

3) Rotation & SLA:
- DEK rotation is handled by Redwood (you can set interval). Master key rotation is handled in your KMS; when you rotate the master key, we rewrap DEKs on next access. We support immediate rewrap on rotation requests.

4) Logging & retention:
- Default request payload retention is 90 days.
- We can configure per-account retention: 0, 7, 30, 90, 365, or custom up to 3650 days.
- Payload logging can be disabled entirely and we provide redacted traces for debugging.

5) Audit & monitoring:
- Key usage logs can be forwarded to your CloudTrail/Stackdriver depending on the integration; we also emit internal audit events (key access, rewraps) that we can include in an audit bundle.

I attached the integration guide for a deeper look (redwood_kms_integration_guide.pdf). Happy to walk through specific AWS KMS policies during the call.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding a few security clarifications from Product Security:

- HSM integration: For the HSM-backed option we support both cloud HSMs and customer-managed on-prem HSMs via PKCS#11 or KMIP. Keys can be configured to be non-exportable. For customers requiring FIPS 140-2 validated HSMs we can work with your vendor (Thales, Gemalto, AWS CloudHSM) as part of a Dedicated/Private deployment.
- Key access logs: We can surface per-key usage logs and, in cloud integrations, forward key usage to your CloudTrail project. For Private deployments we can configure syslog forwarding to your collector.
- Audit artifacts: We can produce a scoped audit bundle (key usage, access control lists, recent rewrap events) and provide SOC 2 Type II evidence after an NDA.
- Data purge: We support on-demand purge of account data and a KV cache purge for specific workloads; please note purge timelines for long-term backups may vary by deployment, we'll document specifics in the SOW.

I'll be on the deep-dive. If you can confirm AWS CMEK for pilot and whether you need HSM for settlement data, we'll prepare the appropriate integration checklist.

Thanks,
